title: 2D Navier-Stokes (Vorticity)
desc.equation: Dimensionless 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in the stream function-vorticity (ψ-ω) formulation:
desc.domain: Depending on the scenario: closed rectangular cavity (validation case with L = H = 1) or channel with an obstacle (cylinder of radius r or w × h rectangle centered at (c_x, c_y), or a step of height h and length l in the lower-left corner). Triangular mesh over a grid of n_x × n_y nodes:
desc.bc.cavity.psi: zero stream function on all walls:
desc.bc.cavity.lid: lid (y = H) with tangential velocity u = 1; the other walls at rest:
desc.bc.cavity.omega: wall vorticity from the generalized Thom's formula, with ψ_nb at the neighboring interior node at distance h and u_tan the wall velocity:
desc.bc.channel.inlet: inlet (x = 0), uniform flow u = 1 and zero vorticity:
desc.bc.channel.obstacle: obstacle (cylinder or rectangle) and step, respectively:
desc.bc.channel.omega: wall and obstacle vorticity from Thom's formula with u_tan = 0;
desc.bc.channel.outlet: outlet (x = L): natural condition for ψ and ω.
desc.method: Finite Element Method with linear triangular elements. At each time step: Poisson equation for ψ, wall vorticity from Thom's formula, element velocities and vorticity transport with a semi-implicit step (explicit convection, implicit diffusion). The fields are redrawn after each group of steps.
desc.reference: Cavity at Re = 100: benchmark by Ghia, Ghia and Shin (1982), with stream function minimum ψ_min ≈ −0.1034 and primary vortex center at (x, y) ≈ (0.6172, 0.7344).
desc.reference.note: The validation case of the undergraduate thesis (TCC) that originated the platform (41 × 41 mesh, Δt = 0.01, 2000 steps) is in the preset selector. There is no reference for the channel with obstacle; the simulation shows only the numerical result.
